summary: Extended the probe one step further into the split-brain symptom. With a bounded wait for the majority side to have its own leader before writing, a native run had both leaders acknowledge a client write while partitioned: both_sides_acknowledged true on the flagged case (the stale-configuration minority leader and the majority-side leader each completed their Apply), and false for the flag-off control, where the isolated side has no leader so only the majority acknowledges. That is the fourth bounded check now declared, with its control, in a successor experiment (previous_id and revision_reason recorded; the derived operand is inspectable in the event). FSM divergence and lost acknowledged entries remain unwitnessed — the applied-slice comparison at the conflict index did not line up and no entry was recovered after healing — so that part of the registered gap stays open and is stated as a limitation. The whole-question interpretation remains violated with defect_claim asserted for the three complete comparisons (configuration loss witness 15/control 18; minority election witness 22/control 25; single-side acknowledgement witness 27/control 29), now noting the concurrent two-sided acknowledgement as under test.
